sheet-1-1.description: An inset in the lower left of sheet 93, an additional sheet of June 1921 that Sanborn added to its South Orange series for Springfield Township, Union County. It shows the grounds of the Baltusrol Golf Club on Shunpike Road, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with its own north arrow, turned so that north points to the upper left. Shunpike Road crosses the inset from side to side with a 50 foot width, and Briant Avenue comes down to it from the north on the right-hand side; a 4 inch water pipe runs south from the junction to a hydrant inside the grounds and a 3 inch pipe branches towards the club buildings. North of the road are a few scattered frame outbuildings, including a stable, a pump house and dwellings in block 1, and a field house stands east of Briant Avenue in block 2. South of the road are the club dormitory, small cottages and, near the bottom of the inset, the clubhouse complex of the Baltusrol Golf Club, a large rambling frame and stucco building with dining room, kitchen and dormitory wings and an auto house with a second-floor dormitory. A note records no watchman, steam heat, electric light and hydrants and hose as shown. The rest of the inset is open ground of the golf course and carries no buildings. The upper half of the sheet is a small-scale key map of the township and the lower right holds a second inset of the Carter Bell Manufacturing Company plant, both outside this part.
notes: Briant Av at the junction with Shunpike Rd is taken to be today's Baltusrol Way; placed from that one junction with the inset's own north arrow and the 100 ft scale, so only roughly placed.
Today's Briant Parkway and Bryant Avenue elsewhere in Springfield are not the street drawn here.

Printed sheet 93 (Add'l sheet, June 1921). Top half: key map of Springfield Township (small scale, not configured). Bottom: two insets, part 1 Baltusrol Golf Club on Shunpike Rd at Briant Av (100 ft), part 2 The Carter Bell Mfg Co heavy acid plant by a creek and the R.V.R.R. (50 ft). The key map (top half) is at small scale and is not georeferenced.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: The Carter Bell Mfg Co heavy acid and sulphur chloride plant, by a creek and the R.V.R.R., near the Summit line (50 ft) (no street junction; Rahway Valley RR is abandoned (not usable as control); needs hand-picked control from parcel corners of the plant site or the old R.V.R.R. curve (step 6b)).

sheet-2.description: Sheet 94 of the June 1921 additional sheets for Springfield Township, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. It covers the northern approach to the village along Morris Avenue, a 60 foot road that runs from the top of the sheet down past Short Hills Avenue to the corner of Salter Street and Morrison Road at the bottom. Baltusrol Way crosses the top of the sheet, curving to the right edge, and Short Hills Avenue runs east from Morris Avenue past a row of frame dwellings on narrow lots lettered B to M. West of Morris Avenue a large irregular tract (block 1) holds a dwelling with outbuildings, two brick-veneered stores marked old and a stable; a brook runs down from the top of the sheet behind it and another crosses the open block 2 on the east side diagonally to the lower right edge. In the lower left Proffit, a short street of small lots, leaves Morris Avenue westward, and Briant Avenue curves across the bottom left to Salter, with a second stream along it. The bottom of the sheet shows blocks 3, 5 and 6 between Briant Avenue, Salter, Morris Avenue and Morrison Road, built up with frame dwellings, a carpenter shop and garages. Water pipes of 2, 6 and 8 inches and several hydrants are drawn in the streets. Much of the east side is open ground marked only with block numbers 2 and 4, and the margins show where sheets 83, 95 and 96 continue.
notes: Baltusrol Way of 1921 meets Morris Avenue where today's Baltusrol Avenue does; the modern Baltusrol Way is a different road further west.
Proffit is today's Profitt Avenue.
Interstate 78 now cuts through the lower part of the area shown.
Printed sheet 94, 100 ft. Morris Av north of the centre: Short Hills Av, Baltusrol Way, Proffit, Briant Av, Salter, Morrison Rd.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 95 of the June 1921 additional sheets for Springfield Township, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points about 45 degrees to the right of the top. The Rahway Valley Railroad runs down the left side of the sheet beside Tooker Avenue, a long straight 50 foot road lined with frame dwellings, coops and garages on deep lots lettered down its east side. Between them, near the bottom, is the yard of the Union County Coal and Lumber Company with coal pockets, lumber sheds and a siding. A brook crosses the sheet from the left, under Tooker Avenue and a stone bridge, to join a second brook that runs down the right side past the end of Briant Avenue. Westfield Avenue crosses the bottom of the sheet, with Morris Parkway leaving it southward; at its east end Westfield Avenue turns north-east over a stone bridge towards Brook, while Flemer Avenue continues east along the bottom edge with buried gasoline tanks and a concrete bridge. The right side shows the west ends of Salter Street and Keeler Street at Brook, and Trivett Avenue S., Trivett Avenue N., Trivett Avenue and Center Street near the village centre. The large middle of the sheet, block 5, is open land with a few dwellings, and the margins point to sheets 94 and 96.
notes: Westfield Av west of the fork is today's Mountain Avenue; the arm running north-east from the fork to Brook is today's Caldwell Place; Flemer Av is today's Mountain Avenue.
The Rahway Valley Railroad is abandoned today.
Drawn at a different rotation from sheets 94 and 96 (north about 45 degrees right of the top).
Printed sheet 95, 100 ft. Tooker Av and the Rahway Valley R.R. west of the centre, Westfield Av, Flemer Av, Brook, Briant Av.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 96 of the June 1921 additional sheets for Springfield Township, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right, showing the centre of Springfield village. Morris Avenue runs down the middle of the sheet from Morrison Road at the top to Linden Avenue at the bottom. West of it is a grid of residential blocks between Salter, Keeler, Westfield Avenue, Center and Flemer Avenue, bounded on the left by Brook and the short Trivett Avenue streets; the Public School stands on Westfield Avenue and a site is marked for a town hall at Trivett Avenue. Along Morris Avenue are the commercial buildings of the village: a hotel, stores, a barber, a hardware store, a bowling alley, an auto repair shop on Westfield Avenue and a row of brick stores at Flemer Avenue. A brook crosses the sheet from the right edge under Morris Avenue and runs along Flemer Avenue. Main runs east from Morris Avenue past a cemetery, and a second cemetery lies south of Flemer Avenue. The lower part of the sheet holds the F. and F. Nurseries with a packing house, sheds and greenhouses, and in the lower left corner the ends of Montour Avenue, Maryland Avenue and Wabena Avenue, which continue on sheet 97. Water pipes, mostly 6 inch, run in the streets. The right side is largely open land of block 4, and the margins point to sheets 94, 95, 97, 98 and 71.
notes: Westfield Av is today's Caldwell Place; Flemer Av is today's Mountain Avenue; Wabena Av is Wabeno Avenue (printed Wabeno on sheet 97).
Hannah Street junctions sat 4 to 5 m from today's, so Hannah was left out of the control.
Main of 1921 runs roughly where Church Mall is today; the centre was rebuilt around Interstate 78 and Route 24.
Printed sheet 96, 100 ft. Springfield centre: Morris Av from Salter St to Linden Av, Westfield Av (now Caldwell Place), Flemer Av (now Mountain Avenue), Center, Hannah, Trivett, Main. Pilot sheet.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 97 of the June 1921 additional sheets for Springfield Township, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. It covers the area south of the village centre between Morris Avenue on the right edge and the Rahway River on the left. The upper half is a newly platted subdivision of long narrow lots in blocks 1 to 6, laid out along Montour Avenue, Maryland Avenue, Linden Avenue and Springfield Avenue, with Owaissa Avenue and Wabeno Avenue crossing them; apart from one dwelling it is still empty. A garage with a gasoline tank stands at the corner of Springfield Avenue and Morris Avenue. The middle of the sheet is open land (block 7) with a barn and a few dwellings near Morris Avenue, and Colonial Terrace, a 20 foot lane, runs west from Morris Avenue. Further south are the greenhouses of Conrad Wetzel and William Wetzel. The lower part is built up along Battle Hill Avenue and Washington Avenue with frame dwellings on small lots with street numbers, and Riverside Drive follows the Rahway River on two sides of block 9 to Angell Avenue at the bottom edge. A concrete bridge carries Morris Avenue over the river in the lower right. Six inch water pipes run in Morris Avenue, Battle Hill Avenue and Washington Avenue. The margins point to sheets 96 and 98.
notes: Springfield Av on this sheet is today's Meisel Avenue.
Battle Hill Av is today's Battlehill Avenue.
Maryland Av and Montour Av do not survive under those names.

Printed sheet 97, 100 ft. South of the centre: Springfield Av (now Meisel Avenue), Linden, Maryland, Owaissa, Wabeno, Morris Av, Colonial Terrace, Battle Hill, Washington, Riverside Drive, Angell Av; Rahway River.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 98 of the June 1921 additional sheets for Springfield Township, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. It covers the east side of the village from Morris Avenue, which runs down the left edge, to the Essex County and Union County line, which follows a brook down the right half of the sheet. Main runs along the top, curving to the right edge, with the First Presbyterian Church, the Methodist Episcopal Church and its graveyard, dwellings and a plumber's shop on its south side. Below them two short lanes, A Place and B Lane, both marked arbitrary, serve a few dwellings. Springfield Avenue leaves Morris Avenue diagonally towards the lower right corner, crossing the brook at the county line, with an auto repair shop and a printing shop near its start; Maple Avenue runs east from Morris Avenue to meet it, with a machine shop and a row of dwellings on narrow lots. Linden Avenue, Springfield Avenue and Maryland Avenue are drawn entering from the left, and Colonial Terrace and Battle Hill Avenue at the lower left. Much of the sheet is open land in blocks 4 and 11 with scattered houses, coops and sheds; beyond the county line a few buildings belong to sheet 72 of Millburn. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches run in Main, Morris Avenue and Springfield Avenue. The margins point to sheets 71, 72, 96 and 97.
notes: A Pl. and B Lane are marked arbitrary: names assigned by the map maker.
Springfield Av east of Morris Av is partly today's Springfield Avenue and partly today's Maple Avenue; the 1921 Maple Av junction with it has no modern counterpart.
Springfield Av west of Morris Av is today's Meisel Avenue.
Control is along Morris Avenue only (two detected and three hand-picked junctions), so the placement away from Morris Avenue is uncertain.
Printed sheet 98, 100 ft. East of the centre: Morris Av, Main St, Maple Av, Springfield Av, Arbitrary Pl and Lane; Essex/Union county line along the brook.
